title: Tighten CSP script-src (currently 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval') or document the tradeoff
description: VERIFIED: server/main.py SecurityHeadersMiddleware + web/nginx.conf both set script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'. unsafe-eval is required by the live-TV player stack (mpegts.js contains new Function("return this"); verified in node_modules/mpegts.js/dist/mpegts.js) and unsafe-inline by React hydration, but this combination defeats most XSS mitigations. TRADEOFF DOCUMENTED 2026-07-31 in SECURITY_AUDIT.md finding #3 (hls.js/shaka dists do NOT eval directly). REMAINING: runtime audit to scope 'unsafe-eval' to the mpegts chunk only (nonce-based CSP is the eventual goal).

title: Verify stream preflight latency and CDN behavior at runtime
description: VERIFIED CODE (session 2026-07-31): preflight_stream() in server/routes/stream_core.py opens a short aiohttp connection (status check + 1-byte read) before every live/VOD/remux/transcode/proxy StreamingResponse so dead channels return 502 instead of 200-with-empty-body; results are cached short-TTL (30s success / 5s failure) keyed by URL+Range, with env-configurable STREAM_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT. Unit + route tests added (test_stream.py, test_stream_live.py TestPreflightFailure, test_stream_vod.py TestPreflightFailure) and passing — full backend suite 1379 pass / 17 skip / 3 xfail. Remaining risk: verify against the real provider (iptv-provider.example.com) that (a) channel zapping latency is acceptable with the cache, (b) the 1-byte read does not desync mpegts.js, (c) dead channel IDs (e.g. 250, 1) now return 502 quickly.
